item.title: October 2026 CVE Landscape
item.content:encoded: In October 2026, Insikt Group® identified 82 high-impact vulnerabilities to prioritize for remediation, 52 of which had a Very Critical Recorded Future Risk Score. This represents a 13% decrease from the 94 vulnerabilities reported in September.36 of October’s high-impact CVEs were surfaced through the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, 33 were reported in open sources and validated by Insikt Group, and 13 were exclusively surfaced through honeypot data.The 82 vulnerabilities in this report affected products from 51 vendors, with Citrix and Microsoft together accounting for approximately 15% of the vulnerabilities. The remaining exposure spanned network edge and security management appliances; operating systems and endpoint software; collaboration, content management, and enterprise platforms; and artificial intelligence (AI), developer, and automation tools.Insikt Group created a Nuclei template to detect the two PHP2Shell vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619). Insikt Group also published templates for CVE-2026-87902 (WordPress) and CVE-2026-86124 (AutoAgent). These are available to customers in the Recorded Future Intelligence Operations Platform.Quick reference: October 2026 vulnerability tableAll 69 vulnerabilities below were actively exploited or operationally weaponized in October 2026.This table does not include the 13 CVEs that were exclusively surfaced through honeypot data, which are available to Recorded Future Intelligence Platform customers via the CVE Monthly report.The table below also provides examples of public PoCs identified by Insikt Group. These PoCs were not tested for accuracy or efficacy. Vulnerability management teams should exercise caution and verify the validity of PoCs before testing.Palo Alto Networks PAN-OSBeyondTrust Remote SupportEG Secure Solutions SiteGuard Server EditionCollabora Online (CODE Server)Arista VeloCloud OrchestratorAtlassian Data Center and server productsAdobe Commerce and Magento Open SourceCisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD SoftwareCisco Secure Email GatewayCitrix NetScaler ADC and GatewayVanderbilt University REDCapIvanti Pulse Connect SecureMicrosoft SharePoint ServerPalo Alto Networks PAN-OSMicrosoft SharePoint ServerMicrosoft SharePoint ServerMicrosoft SharePoint ServerList of vulnerabilities that were actively exploited in October 2026 based on Recorded Future data (excluding honeypot-sourced CVEs).PHP2Shell reporting covered confirmed honeypot shell execution, a Fragnesia chain yielding root access on 25 servers, and Potassium-associated payload attempts. Other PHP2Shell activity involved suspected preparations for a North Korean attack, which was assessed with moderate confidence as linked to the Lazarus Group. Other exploitation activity this month included Longlegs deploying Warlock ransomware; ransomware groups exploiting PAN-OS; CL-STA-0954 targeting Fortinet products for data theft; PEERSTITCH deployment; Integrity Technology Group-enabled espionage; CyberXero’s AI-assisted exploitation; and ClingSTUN deployment.37 of the 82 vulnerabilities enabled remote code execution (RCE). Collaboration, content-management, and enterprise platforms were the most affected product type, with 12 vulnerabilities. Microsoft had the largest vendor share, with three vulnerabilities.Insikt Group identified public proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits or scanners for 37 of the 82 vulnerabilities in this report.The most common weakness class was CWE-78 (OS Command Injection), with eight vulnerabilities, followed by CWE-287 (Improper Authentication), with seven. CWE-22 (Path Traversal) and CWE-77 (Command Injection) each affected six vulnerabilities.10 of the 82 vulnerabilities were at least five years old, and the oldest was approximately 16 years old.PHP2Shell exploitation enables root access and internal pivotingIn October, two vulnerabilities in PHP, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (collectively referred to as “PHP2Shell”), drew attention from threat actors, who also chained them with CVE-2026-46300, a Linux kernel vulnerability known as Fragnesia. Following their disclosure, Insikt Group published multiple notes and detection rules involving PHP2Shell in October. Highlights from our coverage include:Root access and internal pivoting: A TTP Instance detailed a campaign chaining CVE-2026-109618 (PHP) and CVE-2026-109619 (PHP) with CVE-2026-46300 (Linux kernel), also known as Fragnesia. Dream Research reported root access on 25 servers, including systems in a US government-affiliated environment. PHP2Shell provided initial access, and Fragnesia enabled privilege escalation. The actor deployed web shells, stole configurations, credentials, and private keys, and maintained reverse Secure Shell (SSH) tunnels to internal systems, enabling service-account password decryption and Active Directory enumeration. Domain-account creation was attempted but not confirmed.Technical analysis and exploit development: A separate TTP Instance explained PHP2Shell’s memory-lifecycle failures enabling unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE), highlighting Apache mod_php exposure and unvalidated early PoCs. Separate TTP Instances covering reports from SOCRadar and AkatsukiLegion described actor-staged exploits, prerequisite checks, and a memory-leak-to-command-execution chain.Threat actor pre-positioning: Two other TTP Instances covered PHP2Shell tooling on an extortion actor’s staging server and CYFIRMA’s assessment of suspected North Korean preparations using 21 compromised nodes to check 216 hosts. CYFIRMA assessed a Lazarus Group connection with moderate confidence. Neither earlier shared-hosting intrusions nor attack preparations established a successful PHP2Shell compromise. A TTP Instance covering Arctic Wolf and Cisco Talos described probes and payload-download attempts associated with Potassium, a Mirai-derived botnet. In separate TTP Instances covering Linux bots reported by Joe Security and Nextron Research, Insikt Group corroborated remote-shell, evasion, and denial-of-service capabilities in the former, and PHP2Shell testing, scanning, downloads, and persistence in the latter. These findings did not confirm successful malware delivery through PHP2Shell. Insikt Group created Sigma rules for Linux and Windows to detect web or PHP workers spawning shells, including PowerShell, and Suricata and Snort rules for multipart session-ID and upload-progress requests. Network detection requires visible HTTP bodies. Correlate these alerts with process creation, worker errors, and outbound activity because individual matches can be benign.Separate PHP vulnerability: A TTP Instance reported on CVE-2026-115560 (PHP), a vulnerability distinct from PHP2Shell that could enable unauthenticated RCE in applications switching session serializers while upload progress is enabled. No in-the-wild exploitation was established at the time of publication. PHP recommended disabling session upload progress pending a separate fix; the initial PHP2Shell patches did not address this vulnerability.

item.title: The Shift: Rethinking the Human in the Loop
item.content:encoded: Ensuring that there are "humans in the loop" is the gold safety standard for making sure artificial intelligence (AI) agentic systems act safely, ethically, and legally. However, as automated processes accelerate and scale, humans lose the ability to provide meaningful oversight over machine-speed workflows. Rather than simply inserting a human into a machine process, leaders must engineer systems that enable AI agents to operate at machine speed while ensuring they act within human-authorized intent, appropriate controls, and safety and legal boundaries. This means thinking strategically about where acceleration is possible and where slowing down to human speed is necessary to avoid catastrophic risk.The Hiring Automation “Doom Loop” Is a WarningHiring offers an instructive example of how humans can be sidelined by a process accelerated by unchecked automation. Machine-assisted decision-making has long been used in the hiring process to manage volume and improve fairness and efficiency. However, generative AI has made reading and writing job applications almost completely machine-dominated, leading the CEO of Greenhouse, a human resources platform, to declare that AI had created a "doom loop" in hiring. No one intended to create this doom loop, but the adoption of automation in one area led to accelerated adoption in others, ultimately sidelining humans from hiring decisions.The hiring doom loop is driven by two mutually reinforcing trends: more applicants are applying for each position, and more companies are relying on automation to sift through the growing volume of applications. Applicants per hire tripled between 2021 and 2024, according to one survey of hiring managers, and Greenhouse reported a 412% increase in applicants per post. Applicants are almost certainly using generative AI to spin up customized applications to hundreds of jobs at once.Meanwhile, 91% of HR departments report using AI in recruitment, and Greenhouse data shows that the number of human recruiters has dropped by over 50%. The recruiters who remain cannot meaningfully evaluate any single application at this volume, further reducing human decision-making in the hiring process. Some companies now use AI to conduct interviews, meaning applicants may not meet an actual human at the company until very late in the process, if at all.Despite the intention of using AI to improve efficiency and manage scale, only one-third of recruiters reported improvements in time-to-hire using AI, while 25% reported it got slower. More companies are lengthening probationary periods, a sign that they're increasingly unable to identify unsuitable candidates before hiring them. Many job hunters express frustration with encountering bots instead of real humans at their potential future employer. At the same time, scammers and state-sponsored cybercriminals have taken advantage of this automated landscape to advance candidates whose real objective is to steal secrets or cryptocurrency.A few factors made hiring one of the first processes to fall victim to the doom loop. Hiring managers were early adopters of automation, using technology like keyword-based filters to parse resumes. At the same time, successful cover letters and resumes tend to follow a formula, which makes them easy to convincingly replicate with generative AI. However, there are two factors that are not unique to hiring that make it susceptible to doom loop dynamics:Incentives for speed and scale: as competition increases, candidates are rewarded for applying to more jobs, faster.Mutually reinforced automation: as application volume outgrew what individuals could manage, automation spread further into the hiring process. This, in turn, drives candidates to prioritize impressing the bots rather than their future human co-workers.The hiring doom loop is a valuable case study for managing automation because it forces leaders to account for factors outside of their direct control. Instead of responding to machine volume with more automation, developers must think strategically about the intended outcomes and potential second-order effects to ensure systems remain aligned with human intent.

item.title: The Classics Return: Vulnerable E-Mail Scripts, (Wed, Nov 4th)
item.source: SANS Internet Storm Center, InfoCON: green
item.content:encoded: One of the early web application vulnerabilities I remember was CVE-2000-0411 [CVE]. This was a simple vulnerability in a CGI-bin script used to send e-mail. The vulnerability was pretty straightforward: Adding additional parameters to the URL leaked environment variables. Other vulnerabilities allowed setting the "To" address and were heavily abused by spammers. And if parameters were passed directly to the sendmail binary, similar vulnerabilities could allow arbitrary code execution.
